body:
> **Now primarily tracked in-repo at `workshop/issues/000004-pre-commit-review-hook.md`** — this issue remains as a public-visibility stub per the ariadne in-repo-first convention. The original spec is preserved below.

---

## Goal

The `review.md` sub-skill is now in place — every commit to shared substrate (candidates/ / elections/ / controversies/) should pass through it with a different AI stack before merging. But the convention is operator-driven; we need tooling to make it enforceable + queryable.

## What's needed

- [ ] **Pre-commit hook** that fails the commit if any new/modified file in candidates/ / elections/ / controversies/ doesn't have a matching review-pass=true entry in a recent `reviews/<year>/*.md` file
- [ ] **reviews/COVERAGE.md** maintained by hand (or by a script) tracking:
  - Which (state, year) batches have been reviewed
  - Which producing-stack made them
  - Which reviewer-stack reviewed them
  - Any unfixed blockers
- [ ] **Cross-stack-coverage policy**: if producing-stack and reviewer-stack are both Claude, count as "incomplete" — flag for a different-stack re-review
- [ ] **CI integration**: GitHub Actions that runs a lint pass on PRs (source-hygiene grep + math sanity-check) as a bare-minimum automated review on top of the AI-mediated full review

## Why

The whole "AI-curated not crowdsourced" pitch in the README depends on the substrate being trustworthy. Without enforcement, the review convention erodes — first commit-without-review is a slippery slope. Tooling makes the convention load-bearing.

## Out of scope

Building our own review tool. We use Claude / Codex / Gemini / etc. as the reviewer; we just need state tracking + commit-gate enforcement on top of them.

## Related

- review skill: `review.md` in repo root
- Source repo: this repo
